Source: Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning, Community Data Snapshots 2026, drawing on American Community Survey 2024 estimates. Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

Gage Park is mostly pre-1978 stock, and that changes the setup

84.4 percent of housing units were built before 1970, and the community-area data does not publish a 1978 bucket, so the real pre-1978 share is higher than that by an amount nobody has measured in Gage Park. Stock of that age brings the federal lead-safe renovation rule with it. The rule turns on two things, a build year before 1978 and work that disturbs the paint, and in Illinois EPA enforces it directly instead of a state program doing it.

In practice the rule is about containment and cleanup rather than about paint. In a Gage Park room it sets a threshold of roughly six square feet of disturbed interior paint, twenty square feet outside, and any window replacement or demolition is covered whatever the area. Sanding the casing on one 1938-median window clears that in a few minutes.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Gage Park.

In Gage Park it is worth asking about before the work starts rather than after the sanding has. Ask whoever you hire to say, in plain terms, how they intend to handle it at your particular address.

Certification is a document, not a sentence on a website. It shows as pending below because no number has been supplied. Ask to see it, in Gage Park and everywhere else.

The part of a Gage Park quote that actually varies

With 52 percent of Gage Park prewar and a 1938 median, the ceilings are the part people forget. Old plaster ceilings move, they have usually been patched at least once, and a flat white over the top of that shows every previous repair the moment the light comes across it. They are worth pricing as their own line. At 50.2 percent multi-unit, Gage Park is a building market as much as a house market. Common areas take more abuse and less care than anything inside a unit, and they are usually the thing that has waited longest.

The lines a quote for Gage Park needs to show

  • Containment, not just paint. 84.4 percent of housing in Gage Park was built before 1970, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.
  • Plaster as well as drywall. 52 percent of Gage Park is prewar. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so wall repair is a different line from wall painting.
  • Setup does not shrink with the room. The median unit here is 5.5 rooms. Masking, cutting in and cleanup cost the same in a small room as a large one, so a flat per-room rate is usually wrong in one direction or the other.
  • Per unit, to a date. 50.2 percent of units here are in buildings of two or more. Turnover work is priced per unit and scheduled to a move-out, not to the weather.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is prewar brick and frame: bungalows, cottages and the larger houses that went up on the better streets before the war. The paintable surface outside is porch, cornice, soffit and sash rather than wall. Inside Gage Park it is plaster and original millwork.

Two figures produce that sentence and no others: build year 1938, and a stock that is 46.1 percent detached, 2 percent attached and 50.2 percent in buildings of two or more.

An inference, not a measurement. Neither the Census nor the regional housing data records what a wall in Gage Park is made from, so no percentage is attached to it and none should be. Your own elevation settles it in four seconds from the sidewalk.

Questions

Asked about Gage Park

Do you paint rental units and common areas in Gage Park?

Yes, and it is a real part of the work here rather than an afterthought. 50.2 percent of housing units in Gage Park sit in buildings of two or more, and 4,393 households rent. Turnover repaints get priced per unit and scheduled around a move-out date. Ask for it that way and you will get a number that fits the deadline.

My house in Gage Park is plaster, not drywall. Is that a problem?

It is not a problem, it is a different repair. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so the fix has to address the movement rather than the line. With a 1938 median build year most of Gage Park is plaster over lath on at least some walls and ceilings. Say so when you call, because it changes the time estimate and it is better said before the quote than after.

How quickly can somebody look at it?

Gage Park is 6.8 straight-line miles from the shop, which is close enough that looking at the work and doing the work do not have to be the same trip. That matters most on small jobs, because a repair that is worth doing gets seen instead of being pushed into a bigger job later. Call 708-935-4289.

Is the $236,361 median home value in Gage Park what a job here costs?

They are two different things. $236,361 is a published estimate of home value in Gage Park and nothing more. Cost of work depends on what is on the walls now, how much trim there is and what has to come off before anything goes on, and none of that is knowable from a median.
